item.title: A century of records paints a worrying picture for Europe's bees
item.description: In most parts of Europe, bees have become less widespread during the last 100 years, according to a new study published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Research concludes that Shakespeare wrote 'Edward III' with Marlowe
item.description: Dr. Rory Loughnane, a reader in early modern studies in the School of Humanities, has confirmed "beyond any reasonable doubt" that William Shakespeare was the principal writer of "Edward III" and that it was written in collaboration with his so-called rival and Canterbury's most famous poet and playwright, Christopher Marlowe. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Limited waste collection services in rural communities linked to high microplastic levels in Mekong River
item.description: Plastics are accumulating in ecosystems around the world, and their tiny fragments can collect and carry chemical pollutants and pathogens into plants, animals and people. When fishermen in Cambodia's Mekong River became alarmed about the amounts of plastic they were hauling up with each catch, they reached out to scientists for help. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI challenges math by solving the unsolvable
item.description: Announcements over recent months that artificial intelligence models have cracked previously unsolvable problems are shaking top-level mathematicians to the core, and they are now asking themselves: Where do we come in? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A home sits atop a ruined embankment on Mousuni Island—where cyclones, monsoons, and rising sea levels are reshaping life in India’s Sundarbans. The damage affects mill... Ver más
item.description: A home sits atop a ruined embankment on Mousuni Island—where cyclones, monsoons, and rising sea levels are reshaping life in India’s Sundarbans. The damage affects mill... Ver más How sad Brenda Olynyk Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Unraveling DNA repair: How cells protect their genetic blueprint
item.description: Every cell in the human body faces a chronic challenge: protecting its DNA. Whenever cells divide, their genetic material must be copied accurately. But DNA is continuously under attack, and when damage goes unrepaired, it can threaten genome stability and contribute to the progression of disease. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Christina Koch, astronauta del Artemis II: “No hay nada que te prepare para ver a tu planeta iluminado como si fuera de día”
item.description: Tras completar con éxito el histórico sobrevuelo lunar, se conoció una frase que la astronauta de la NASA pronunció mientras realizaba la misión Artemis II Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: How the aftermath of negotiations turns 'winners' into 'losers,' and vice versa
item.description: At its best, negotiation is the art of mutual value creation. But once created, that value must be capitalized upon in the post-negotiation environment. That means the formal end of negotiations is often only the end of the beginning. Time will tell whether the gains and losses sustained during a negotiation are as solid as they seem when the counterparties get up from the table. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cost-analysis tool allows coastal communities to see and estimate benefits of investing in storm-protection measures
item.description: Today, as part of the official release of California's Fifth Climate Change Assessment, researchers at the University of California, Santa Cruz, have launched a platform, data and tools that community leaders can use to estimate the block-by-block climate risks and the cost-effectiveness of adaptation solutions for reducing coastal damages. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Un satélite ruso persiguió a otro norteamericano que ayuda a Ucrania y llegó a acercarse 200 metros
item.description: El Kosmos-2612 realizó maniobras de aproximación durante varios días alrededor del ICEYE-X36, que proporciona imágenes de alta precisión a Kiev; investigadores analizan una posible amenaza rusa Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: The Orionid meteor shower is coming. Here's how and when to watch
item.description: The Orionids—one of two major meteor showers caused by remnants from Halley's Comet—will peak this week, though a large moon will dim visibility until after it sets late at night. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Jackdaw North Sea gasfield to get go-ahead in blow to climate campaigners
item.description: Move signals Andy Burnham’s commitment to the North Sea industry but threatens to undermine Labour’s green credentials The Jackdaw gasfield will be given the go-ahead on Wednesday, signalling Andy Burnham’s commitment to the North Sea fossil fuel industry and threatening to trigger a row with climate campaigners and Labour MPs. Miatta Fahnbulleh and John Healey, the energy secretary and chancellor respectively, will make the announcement from Aberdeen on Wednesday morning after more than a year of deliberations over whether doing so would violate the UK’s climate commitments. Continue… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Kiran Stacey Policy editor

item.title: PermitAI team delivers a one-stop shop for federal permitting data
item.description: The PermitAI team at the Department of Energy's Pacific Northwest National Laboratory has changed how federal agencies search past environmental permitting decisions. Now it is taking that access one step further with two newly released publicly available resources that give instant access to both past decisions and live government data. Together, they cover the full federal permitting life cycle. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A pulsar's apparent slowdown reveals a rare stellar trio
item.description: Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars, the extremely dense cores left behind when massive stars explode. Astrophysicists have recently observed a pulsar rotating over 300 times per second that appeared to be slowing down unusually quickly. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s SR-1 Freedom Advances with Progress on Nuclear Power Module
item.description: Destined for Mars and beyond, NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will be humanity’s first fission-powered spacecraft to travel outside Earth’s orbit. Announced during NASA’s “Ignition” event, this mission will demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space, and progress is underway on its key element: the nuclear power module. To expedite development of the spacecraft, NASA […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Gary Daines

item.title: Meta pauses Muse sharing after researchers find AI chats on the web
item.description: Meta says it paused a Muse feature that lets you share conversations with the AI assistant after researchers found the URLs publicly available on the web, as reported by Ars Technica. In a report published this week, researchers at the security firm Claroc say they found more than 6,800 Muse links through public DNS records. […] Fuente: The Verge.
item.dc:creator: Emma Roth

item.title: Steering electrons with extreme ultraviolet light—team achieves quantum coherent control
item.description: Light is one of the most powerful tools scientists have for probing matter. By interacting with electrons, light reveals how atoms, molecules and materials are structured and how they evolve in time. Highly energetic ultraviolet and X-ray photons are particularly attractive because they can access electrons located close to atomic nuclei, where each chemical element carries its own distinctive electronic fingerprint. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA experimental Mars helicopter blade designs target longer flights
item.description: NASA researchers are developing the future of flight on Mars, laying the groundwork for helicopters with the ability to fly higher and farther while conducting science on the Red Planet. Using high-fidelity computer simulations and wind tunnel tests, engineers are reimagining the rotorcraft blades that could carry the next generation of Mars flyers. Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Raman barcodes' distinguish 20 SARS-CoV-2 variants by their RNA architecture
item.description: A research team led by distinguished professor Giuseppe Pezzotti at the Biomedical Engineering Center, Kansai Medical University (Japan), has demonstrated that differences in the molecular structures of viral RNA can be captured as "Raman barcodes," enabling the identification of 20 SARS-CoV-2 variants and subvariants. These findings are expected to contribute to the development of a rapid method for identifying newly emerging viral variants. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Workplace narcissists crave more than a quiet raise
item.description: According to a new study, all employees like private rewards—a salary increase or glowing performance review that's not broadcast to others in the workplace—but narcissists also want to have rewards made public for their colleagues to see, the researchers found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Los "palillos chinos" de SpaceX tendrán copia china: Deep Blue Aerospace los quiere para su cohete Nebula-2
item.description: La compañía china Deep Blue Aerospace acaba de anunciar que el tanque de propelente de acero inoxidable de 5 metros de diámetro de su cohete Nebula-2 ya ha salido de la línea de montaje. Es un tanque que bate un récord de tamaño dentro del sector privado espacial chino. Sin embargo, hay algo aún más llamativo que el propio tanque: el sistema de recuperación de Nebula-2. Y es que el objetivo de Deep Blue Aerospace no es otro que recuperar la primera etapa del cohete en pleno vuelo, usando unos palillos, similares al sistema Mechazilla de SpaceX. Hasta ahora, este hito solo ha sido logrado por… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: 'Bomb carbon' in wood shavings helped researchers measure the stability of biochar in soil
item.description: Biochar can store carbon in the soil and reduce the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere—yet we still know too little about how long the biochar will persist. Now, researchers from the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences have found a new way to measure this, using wood from the 1960s that was affected by nuclear weapons testing. The paper is published in the journal Radiocarbon. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Civic laboratories': How online spaces are reshaping civic engagement among Gen Z
item.description: Even before they are old enough to vote, some young people are finding ways to make a difference. Civic engagement among youth ages 15 to 25 can range from volunteering in the community and joining a protest march to signing a petition or expressing political views on social media, according to Portland State University researcher Yue Ni. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Individual atomic collisions can now be detected in the lab, potentially opening up pathways to new physics
item.description: Tiny atoms and molecules are constantly bombarding each other all around us. While we regularly measure the large-scale effects of these interactions, measuring the effect of each individual collision is far more difficult. But now, researchers have managed to measure how tiny gas particles affect a single silica particle in the lab. In their new study, published in Physical Review Letters, the team describes how they detected the momentum transfers of individual collisions of gas particles with a nanoparticle levitated in laser light. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Drones help archaeologists find Aboriginal rock art sites hidden in Australia's rugged Blue Mountains
item.description: Drone-mounted laser technology is helping archaeologists locate Aboriginal rock art sites hidden in the rugged, densely vegetated landscapes of Australia's Blue Mountains, demonstrating a new approach to surveying archaeological sites that can be difficult and expensive to reach on foot. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Marital breakups can also have long-term effects, and some are felt keenly in old age
item.description: Marital breakups have consequences that extend beyond the immediate end of cohabitation. Research from the University of Granada has found that these consequences can last for decades, eventually becoming a significant source of vulnerability as people reach old age—especially if they live alone and have little contact with their children or insufficient social support. The study, published in the International Journal of Sociology, was conducted by Juan López Doblas, a professor in the Department of Sociology, and María del Pilar Díaz Conde, a professor in the Department of Social Psychology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Eighteen years of whale call research reveals key habitat of mysterious species
item.description: In a boost for the conservation of one of the world's most elusive and least-understood whale species, researchers analyzing more than 18 years of underwater acoustic recordings collected off northwest Australia have discovered that Omura's whales are most likely to be found in warm, food-rich waters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hot plasma may explain how rapidly feeding black holes launch powerful jets
item.description: Some supermassive black holes rapidly consume surrounding matter while simultaneously firing powerful streams of plasma into space at nearly the speed of light. However, this creates a physical puzzle: rapid feeding is expected to form a cold, flat accretion disk around the black hole, which prevents powerful jets from forming. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Largest collection of Roman cave inscriptions discovered in Spain
item.description: Archaeologists have uncovered the largest collection of Latin cave inscriptions anywhere in the Roman Empire. Early analysis of the inscriptions discovered at Cova Dones reveals that a female deity was worshipped at the site and that women had a prominent role in rituals there—highly unusual in Roman society. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The road to discovery: DNA in the air maps biodiversity
item.description: Curtin University researchers have detected traces of hundreds of plants and animals by collecting DNA from the air as they drove more than 1,100km (684 miles) across Western Australia. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Employees with autism report hidden labor of workplace camouflaging in new study
item.description: Employees with autism may expend considerable time and effort modifying their behavior to meet workplace expectations, from rehearsing conversations and monitoring facial expressions to concealing sensory discomfort, according to a new study led by a Penn State researcher. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Collecting phones during college lessons raises grades, large randomized trial finds
item.description: Your phone vibrates, a notification pops up, or you just take a quick glance at the screen. Even minor interruptions can affect your concentration—not least when you're in class. Now, a large randomized trial involving more than 16,000 students in India shows that teaching without access to mobile phones can improve students' academic performance. The researchers also found that students who experience phone-free teaching firsthand become more supportive of the restrictions. The research is published in Science. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum probability can't be derived without assuming it first
item.description: For nearly a century, physicists have relied on the Born rule to calculate the chances of different outcomes when they measure a quantum system. Yet despite decades of effort, nobody has managed to derive the rule from more basic mathematical principles without making assumptions about probability along the way. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover a promising blood sugar–regulating compound in red alga
item.description: It is a dietary staple found in sushi, rice wraps and ramen toppings. Commonly known as nori in Japan and gim in Korea, red seaweed is especially popular across Asia. Yet, despite its widespread consumption, many of its nutritional benefits remain poorly understood. Now, research led by Hokkaido University scientists has discovered that digestion of a particular red alga releases a peptide, or a small fragment of protein, with potential benefits for blood glucose control and diabetes prevention. The study was published in Food Bioscience. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Provides Progress Update on Moon Base Rovers
item.description: As NASA works to build the Moon Base, crewed and robotic lunar rovers will play a crucial role during early development through technology demonstrations, astronaut transport, terrain mapping, scientific investigations, and resource prospecting. Data from these early missions will inform future mobility systems and infrastructure needed for astronauts to live and work on the Moon. […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Surprising pattern emerges in reincarnation reports
item.description: An analysis of more than 1,600 cases of purported reincarnation has revealed a striking correlation: The time between death and "rebirth" was shorter on average when records indicated that the prior person had died unexpectedly. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A quantum pathway to entropy-free energy transfer
item.description: For scientists, breakthroughs often stem from unexpected turns. A research team led by Oscar Dahlsten, an associate professor in the Department of Physics at City University of Hong Kong (CityUHK), set out to prove a theoretical limitation, only to discover a quantum solution. The finding breaks traditional physical constraints and introduces a strategy for harvesting energy from fluctuating sources. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Webb Captures Stellar Jets
item.description: An image from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Oct. 6, 2026, reveals a cauldron of cosmic creation. Webb has unveiled numerous stars formerly hidden by clouds of dust in a stellar nursery known as NGC 7129, which resides about 3,300 light-years from Earth. Learn more about this region – and tour it in […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: Study asks, Who benefits from where hospitals or landfills are located?
item.description: Cities are built around critical public facilities, some more desirable for neighbors than others. People want to live near hospitals and parks. Living near a wastewater plant or a landfill is another matter. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Locusts get a sensory assist from nanomaterials—helping them detect more chemicals
item.description: Scientists have long explored the idea of using insects as our agents in the field in places where humans won't fit or survive. Imagine a cockroach in an earthquake zone, able to skitter into the rubble to map out exactly where human chemical signatures can be found, or a grasshopper leaping through a minefield to bring back a map of the bombs based on the vapors it encountered. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Welcomes Uzbekistan as Newest Artemis Accords Signatory
item.description: The Republic of Uzbekistan became the 77th signatory of the Artemis Accords during a ceremony in Samarkand on Monday, committing to the practical principles that guide safe, transparent, and responsible civil space exploration. “Uzbekistan joins the Artemis Accords at a pivotal moment,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. “President Trump has directed NASA to build […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Shaw

item.title: Study links gambling ads to betting activity, searches for help
item.description: From social media feeds to sports broadcasts, gambling ads have become increasingly difficult to avoid. New CU Boulder research links gambling advertising to more gambling activity and more searches for help with problem gambling. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Peat bogs, the natural archives of mining fallout, reveal ancient Europe's hidden metal networks
item.description: For thousands of years, humans shaped their world with stone, wood and bone. Metallurgy, the art and science of working with metals such as copper, bronze and iron, marked a turning point in human history. The mining that fueled metalworking also shaped Europe's and the Mediterranean's economies and politics over centuries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Octopus-inspired patch grips skin and reveals pulse through shifting colors
item.description: It looks like a small, transparent patch with a rainbow on its surface—or for those old enough to remember, the back of a CD. The patch is the first of its kind in the world and, when combined with an ordinary smartphone camera, can measure two things: pulse and blood vessel stiffness. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New analytical method reveals what happens inside tiny molecular frameworks
item.description: Tiny magnetic probes can be used to investigate the chemical forces at work inside the pores of molecular framework compounds, but until now, this had only been possible to a limited degree. A new method developed by a team at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (MLU) could help to better understand the properties of these materials and control these properties in the future. The study is published in the journal Small. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What is Discovery Loop, Chinese teen AI prodigy Nathan Chen’s rumoured next destination?
item.description: Just days after announcing his departure from Moonshot AI, teen Chinese artificial intelligence prodigy Nathan Chen Guangyu seems to have found his next destination. On Tuesday, Arfur Grok, a widely-watched anonymous social media account that tracks AI talent movements in the US, posted that the former Moonshot AI researcher was joining Discovery Loop, an AI start-up founded by four former Google senior researchers including former chief scientist Jeff Dean. Launched just two months ago, the... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Chow

item.title: Could wood provide a better home for oil-degrading microbes?
item.description: According to a study conducted by researchers at Sultan Qaboos University, the material used to support microbial biofilms could influence their potential role in treating water generated during oil production. The research was led by Ph.D. candidate Arwa Al-Hadhrami under the supervision of Dr. Daniel Blackburn and conducted by a Sultan Qaboos University team representing the College of Agricultural and Marine Sciences and the Water Research Center, Oman. The results are published in Environmental Advances. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Octopus and cuttlefish suckers may have evolved by repurposing ancient developmental genes
item.description: Cephalopods, like the octopus, have specialized arms and suckers, but how these structures evolved from the simple bodies of their mollusk ancestors remains a mystery. Researchers from the University of Tokyo compared gene activity during embryonic development of cuttlefish, octopus and snail body parts. They found that several genes associated with appendage patterning showed expression along developing cephalopod arms, but no comparable patterns in developing suckers. Developing suckers instead expressed Ets1, a gene associated with early embryonic development in mollusks. The findings… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Giant canyon on Mars is still tectonically active today
item.description: Scientists at Columbia University and Imperial College London have found that the largest canyon system in the solar system is still active and shaping Mars today, billions of years after it first formed. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers explore the valuable connection between birds, memory and territory in Chile
item.description: Black-necked swans, spot-flanked gallinules, southern lapwings, austral thrushes and dozens of other bird species fly across the Río Cruces Wetland, carrying the biocultural memory of the territory. Both resident birds and species that migrate throughout the year bear witness to the many changes this landscape has undergone over time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage. Using advanced imaging technology, researchers discovered that statins can attach to a crucial protein in muscle cells and force open a channel that normally controls calcium flow. This causes calcium to leak continuously, potentially damaging muscle tissue. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Added receptor helps CAR T cells stay in bone marrow in cancer mouse models
item.description: By turning a patient's own immune cells into stronger cancer-fighting cells, CAR T-cell therapy has transformed how some blood cancers are treated. But it's been harder to extend this approach to solid tumors, including cancer that has spread to the bone. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains
item.description: A new study reveals that improved hurricane forecast graphics may help people identify threatened areas without making them more likely to recognize the danger or take protective action. Researchers also found that a widespread misunderstanding of the hurricane cone persists, highlighting a potentially dangerous gap between accurate forecasts and public preparedness. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Keeping jumping genes in place: New role for protein complex discovered
item.description: As much as half of the human genome is composed of so-called "jumping genes." These DNA sequences can make copies of themselves that are inserted back into the genome at another location, playing a significant functional role in creating the diversity that drives evolution and in regulating how other genes are turned on or off. However, their jumps can also make the genome less stable and create mutations that have been associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, autoimmune disease and cancer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe’s first five minutes
item.description: Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe’s earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world’s most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen
item.description: Scientists have identified the “fattest” belemnite ever discovered, a bizarre, barrel-shaped squid relative that lived in Wyoming’s ancient seas 160 million years ago. The exceptionally rare fossils reveal a creature unlike anything previously known, potentially a predator of smaller squid-like animals and a surprising survivor of a supposedly vanished family. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Psychological symptoms may drive menopause-related workforce attrition
item.description: Turnover related to menopause has become a critical global socioeconomic challenge, affecting female career longevity and organizational productivity. A new study suggests that, although many employers have attempted to make special accommodations in the workplace, they fail to address a woman's increased psychological burdens related to the menopause transition. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The sun may have stripped away meters of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS
item.description: The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS brought material from another planetary system within reach of our telescopes, but reading its chemistry poses a problem. Energetic particles encountered during its journey through space may have changed its outer layers, so how much of what astronomers detect still reflects the comet's birthplace? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover a way to kill dangerous gut bacteria without killing the good
item.description: Scientists have discovered a natural compound that targets dangerous C. difficile bacteria without wiping out the gut's beneficial microbes. Successful early tests suggest it could lead to a gentler, more effective treatment for stubborn intestinal infections that frequently return. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Giving £2 a day to people in the Amazon helps protect rainforest, pilot project finds
item.description: Researchers say almost 90% of participants in unconditional basic income scheme in Peru adopted environmentally beneficial practices A pioneering project to provide Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon with an unconditional basic income has contributed to the protection of the rainforest, according to a study. The analysis from the University of Bath is expected to contribute to a growing debate about the role of direct payments to communities that maintain globally important ecosystems. Continue reading... Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Watts

item.title: Fear study finds AI anxiety among Americans' top fears for the first time
item.description: Chapman University has released the results of its 12th annual Chapman University Survey of American Fears, revealing that concerns about artificial intelligence have entered the nation's top 10 fears for the first time. The survey found that more than half of Americans fear AI could harm the political process, while nearly half worry it will hurt the economy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Measuring regrowth: Erk gradients guide zebrafish fins back to their original size after injury
item.description: In a new Nature Physics study, researchers found that fin regrowth in zebrafish is driven by a brief burst of growth signal at the fin tip, sized to the amount lost, which sets up gradients of Erk activity that guide the regrowth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
item.description: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture. Scientists suggest this change could be an evolutionary adaptation that helps older adults develop wisdom and share decades of knowledge with younger generations. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Study examines suicide awareness among agricultural educators
item.description: As concerns about farmer mental health continue to grow, agricultural researchers are compiling more data on the complex nature of suicide awareness among those who may be able to offer help. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Lucy mission marks 5 years of discoveries
item.description: On Oct. 16, 2021, NASA's Lucy spacecraft began its journey to the never-before-explored Jupiter Trojan asteroids with an early morning launch. Now less than a year away from the first-ever close-up of a Trojan, the Southwest Research Institute–led mission has already made several findings during its first five years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Una misteriosa señal del James Webb en Fornax desconcierta a los astrónomos
item.description: Cuando miramos al cielo, vemos apenas unos cuantos puntitos brillantes sobre un montón de oscuridad. Si tenemos el privilegio de estar en un lugar alejado de la contaminación lumínica , veremos muchos más puntitos o incluso un resplandor borroso y lechoso como el que aparece ante nuestros ojos cuando los posamos en la Vía Láctea. Pero ahí fuera hay mucho más. Los telescopios espaciales se encargan de detectar objetos que el ojo no ve e incluso de desentrañar su composición. Aun así, no pueden verlo todo y a veces descubren sorpresas como la que acaba de sacar a la luz el James Webb al… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Alberto Sánchez ha comentado: This looks like a PS2 cut scene
item.description: Float into the weekend... 🪼 Like a space jellyfish! This fuzzy, glowing "jellyfish" shape in the sky was created when the exhaust plumes from our SpaceX... Fuente: NASA.

item.description: Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Scientists find a way to fight Alzheimer’s brain damage without removing toxic tau
item.description: Scientists have found a promising way to protect the brain from Alzheimer’s-related damage by blocking immune cells that contribute to the destruction of neurons. In mice, the treatment preserved roughly 40% more tissue in memory centers and improved memory, even without removing harmful tau protein buildup. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Near miss: Indonesia probes crash of suspected Chinese rocket fragment
item.description: Indonesian authorities were investigating Tuesday after a car-sized piece of debris, possibly from a Chinese rocket according to a government agency, crashed into a palm oil plantation near homes and work sites. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Japan launches spacecraft to mysterious moons of Mars in a bold mission to bring home soil samples
item.description: Japan launched a spacecraft on Tuesday on a five-year mission to explore Mars' mysterious moons, Phobos and Deimos, and bring back samples for the first time. The $578 million project aims to deliver dust, soil and rocks to Earth in 2031, potentially shedding light on how the moons formed and the origins of life. Publicado también por: France 24 - English. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Deep-sea expedition will revisit Pacific mining site five and a half years after test
item.description: During Oct. 2026, the research vessel SONNE set sail from San Diego into the Pacific Ocean for expedition SO322. Its destination: the Clarion-Clipperton Zone north of the equator—the area that harbors the largest known deposits of polymetallic nodules on the seafloor. Germany, among others, holds an exploration license in this region. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Marine life dramatically declined in Gulf of Mexico in years after BP oil spill, study finds
item.description: In a deep, dark part of the Gulf of Mexico, the number of marine animals plummeted by about 60% in the years following the 2010 Deepwater Horizon explosion, a new study found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Japan launches mission to bring back samples from Mars’s moon Phobos
item.description: Japan’s H3 rocket launched the MMX probe on Tuesday, starting a three-year mission to collect samples from Phobos and study the origins of the Solar System. Publicado también por: Ars Technica, Al Jazeera English, Sky News - World. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: New brain for Galileo
item.description: Twelve Galileo Second Generation (G2) satellites will join the current fleet in the coming years. They will deliver unprecedented positioning, navigation and timing capabilities thanks to an array of new features, including a new signal generation module, the ‘brain' of the spacecraft. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: NASA reveals 16 stunning galaxies hiding cosmic chaos
item.description: NASA's stunning new gallery of 16 galaxies reveals colossal black hole jets, explosive star formation, and spectacular cosmic collisions through the combined power of Chandra, James Webb, Hubble, and other telescopes. These extraordinary images expose the hidden forces shaping galaxies across the universe and offer clues about the Milky Way's own past and future. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between vitamin C and cancer survival
item.description: A surprising clinical trial suggests that taking vitamin C daily could improve survival in people with precancerous blood disorders and early-stage blood cancers. Patients receiving the supplement had fewer adverse events and showed a promising survival advantage, raising hopes that a common vitamin could help protect against leukemia-related complications. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: Human activities have become intertwined with how water is distributed across the continents. A new study brings their effects into sharper focus. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Synthetic public opinion polling: AI personas don't always change their minds like real voters do
item.description: A voter surveyed in October may give a different answer by January. An AI persona might not, depending on how it's built. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists reach the ultimate quantum limit on a surface
item.description: Scientists have achieved a quantum breakthrough by creating an ultra-clean surface where individual molecules can maintain their delicate quantum properties at the fundamental limit. The discovery could unlock unprecedented control over molecules and help drive the next generation of quantum technologies. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NZ's climate in 'uncharted territory,' with more extreme weather events ahead
item.description: Much is being made of a record-strength El Niño event that could well spell a drier, windier summer for the north and east of New Zealand. But, as a major new assessment shows, it is forming against a backdrop of warming that's pushed the country's climate into "uncharted territory." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA solves a strange mystery hidden inside asteroid Bennu’s boulders
item.description: NASA scientists have finally uncovered why asteroid Bennu loses heat so quickly despite being covered in massive boulders. Samples returned to Earth reveal that its rocks are filled with hidden cracks, solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Juvenile striped bass maintaining average abundance in Virginia waters in 2026
item.description: Preliminary results from an ongoing long-term survey conducted by William & Mary's Virginia Institute of Marine Science (VIMS) suggest that an average year class of young-of-year striped bass was produced in the Virginia tributaries of the Chesapeake Bay in 2026. Striped bass are an important top predator in the Chesapeake Bay ecosystem and a valuable resource for commercial and recreational anglers. The 2026 year class, representing fish hatched this spring, will reach fishable sizes in three to four years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Japón lanza la primera misión mundial a una luna de Marte
item.description: Científicos japoneses lanzaron el martes una nave espacial que aspira a ser la primera en recoger muestras de una de las lunas de Marte, lo que podría ayudar a desvelar los orígenes del sistema solar y de la vida en la Tierra. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Nanoscale tech tracks proteins inside living neurons to guide Alzheimer's and Parkinson's drug discovery
item.description: A technology developed at The University of Queensland allowing scientists to observe how disease-related proteins behave inside living neurons will be used to advance early drug discovery for neurodegenerative diseases. The NASTIC (Nanoscale Spatiotemporal Indexing Clustering) platform, spun out into Brisbane-based startup Accretion Bio, enables researchers to study real-time biological processes in living cells across space and time at the single-molecule level for the first time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why painful arthritis can return stronger after cancer treatment
item.description: Researchers discovered that recurring arthritis triggered by cancer immunotherapy may be driven by immune cells that remember previous attacks and return in a more aggressive state. The findings could pave the way for treatments that prevent painful flare-ups while preserving the immune system's ability to fight cancer. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.description: The public K-12 school system in the United States has become pervasively shaped by standardized testing. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: If you've ever created a snowflake by folding, cutting and unfolding a piece of paper, you've practiced the art of kirigami. Like origami, kirigami has inspired innovations far beyond the elementary school classroom, with applications ranging from deployable structures for spacecraft to semiconductors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Molecular switch controls how cells load cargo for recycling
item.description: Cells constantly recycle proteins and other cellular components. But how do they ensure that the right cargo ends up in the right recycling vesicle—one of the cell's transport carriers? A team at the University of Basel has identified a molecular switch that controls this process. The small protein ARF-1 ensures that recyclable cargo is efficiently loaded into transport vesicles and returned to the cell's surface. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Forgotten particle could answer mystery of why we exist, say physicists
item.description: Scientists have unveiled a new theory on the birth of the cosmos, suggesting the early universe was shaped by an ancient particle that has been overlooked for decades. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Criminal justice researchers use statistical modeling to examine wrongful-conviction risk
item.description: A University of Mississippi study is adding nuance to a debate over how often police interrogation tactics can produce false confessions leading to wrongful convictions. In a recent simulation study published in the Journal of Criminal Justice, Ole Miss criminal justice and legal studies professors Mary Catlin and Thomas Bryan Smith found that the predicted likelihood of a false confession grows with the length of a police interrogation. Fuente: Phys.org.
